title: B2B AICC Platform
summary: An internal web service where contact-center agents follow live STT transcription during a call, then review AI analysis and consultation history after it ends.

ownership.label: My role
ownership.description: I designed and implemented the agent and manager web UI, call state, SSE transcription, and connection-recovery experience.

outcome.label: What changed
outcome.description: Agents keep their transcription context and move to the next task even as call, network, and analysis state change.

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description: Agents and managers work with the same call information through different screens. Live transcription and connection status matter during a call; durable history and AI analysis matter after it ends. I designed the frontend screens and state flow so that transition stays continuous.

service.label: Service
service.description: An internal web service that supports contact-center consultation work

users.label: Users
users.description: Agents handling live calls and managers reviewing consultation status and history

role.label: My scope
role.description: Designed and implemented agent and manager web UI, call state, SSE transcription, and connection recovery

constraint.label: Disclosure
constraint.description: External SI and private project; customer data, operational data, internal screens, and performance figures are not disclosed

workflow.title: Primary user flow
workflow.description: Agents follow transcription from the moment a call starts, then review analysis and history in the same context when it ends.

problemTitle: The consultation context had to survive disconnected or out-of-order real-time data.
problemDescription: Call detection, transcription, reconnection, analysis, and role-specific UI affect one another. Building each feature separately makes screen state drift. I connected them through one call-state transition.
implementationTitle: I designed call-state transitions before I designed the screens.
implementationDescription: These four decisions determine how the live consultation UI behaves. Each one explains the problem, the design, and the resulting screen behavior.
frontendFlowAlt: Frontend state flow from active-call polling through call state, SSE, transcript reducer, and consultation UI
frontendFlowCaption: This is the frontend state flow. The UI uses SSE alone while a call is live, then resumes polling after the call ends to find the next call.

callState.title: I switched between polling and SSE through call state.
callState.context: Agents need to find a new call quickly, then follow transcription with no delay once a call begins.
callState.problem: Continuing one-second polling during a call requests data that SSE has already delivered. Two paths can then compete to change the same screen state.
callState.decision: I stored the current and ended call in Zustand and modeled idle, live, and ended. React Query polling runs only while idle or ended; call-scoped SSE owns the latest state while live.
callState.result: The UI finds a new call quickly and uses one real-time path while it is active. It resumes polling when the call ends or recovery fails.
callState.flow: one-second active-call polling → Zustand: idle / live / ended → stop polling while live → call-scoped SSE → resume polling after the call

streamState.title: I translated SSE events into explicit UI state with a reducer.
streamState.context: Partial and finalized speech, call completion, and AI analysis arrive on the consultation screen at different times.
streamState.problem: When partial speech, finalized speech, call completion, and AI analysis arrive through one path, messages can duplicate and ordering or display timing can drift.
streamState.decision: I modeled SNAPSHOT, PARTIAL, FINAL_DISPLAY, CALL_END, and ANALYSIS_COMPLETED or FAILED as reducer events. Partials use speaker-specific temporary slots; finals are deduplicated by conversation ID and sorted by start time.
streamState.result: A newly opened screen restores current state from a snapshot. During a call, it distinguishes partial from finalized speech, while call completion and analysis results use the same state model.
streamState.flow: SSE event → reducer → partial slot or final timeline → CALL_END → analysis pending → completed / failed UI

recovery.title: I made a disconnected stream recoverable for the user.
recovery.context: When the network drops during a call, agents need both the transcription they have already read and a clear connection status.
recovery.problem: SSE can close because of tab changes, network loss, expired authentication, or server termination. Resetting the screen before reconnecting loses transcription the agent has already seen.
recovery.decision: I implemented heartbeat monitoring, staged retry delays with jitter, and manual reconnect. A 401 refreshes the token once before reconnecting, while 403 and 404 become fatal immediately. Reconnect keeps finalized utterances until the next snapshot reconciles them.
recovery.result: Agents can see connection and retry state, and the recovery point stays in the timeline. An unrecoverable close does not leave the UI stuck in live state, so next-call detection continues.
recovery.flow: watchdog heartbeat → retry with jitter → reconnect preserves finals → snapshot reconciliation → recovered marker or terminal handling

roleUi.title: I separated role-specific UI from data responsibilities.
roleUi.context: Agents and managers work with the same call information, but the scope they need to view and control is different.
roleUi.problem: Agents, managers, and administrators use one product but need different access to calls, monitoring, history, and settings. Spreading role conditions through every screen makes later changes difficult.
roleUi.decision: I separated entry through React Router loaders and protected routes. Role-specific slots compose side panels, tabs, and main panels. TanStack Query owns server data, while Zustand owns UI state such as the current call and selections. Each panel also has a skeleton and error boundary.
roleUi.result: The same layout composes the correct UI for each role. A data failure in one panel does not replace the whole screen. Agent and manager capabilities can evolve as separate domains.
roleUi.flow: route loader and role guard → role slots → TanStack Query server state + Zustand UI state → panel-level skeleton and error boundary

architectureTitle: I handled live consultation data and durable history through separate paths.
architectureDescription: The agent screen finds an active call with an authenticated request, then subscribes to call-scoped SSE. After a call ends, it continues with REST-backed analysis and history. The manager screen uses monitoring and history within the same authorization boundary.
architectureAlt: System architecture connecting React agent and manager screens, an internal API, Redis and MariaDB, STT, and external AI analysis
architectureCaption: This is the system context. The frontend separates the live SSE path from the post-call history path so each handles its own kind of data.
resultTitle: I kept the consultation flow continuous as screen state changed.
resultDescription: Agents review transcription, connection recovery, analysis, and history in one flow. I built this experience by making polling, SSE, the reducer, and role-specific UI follow the same state model.
footer: This is a private project. Operational data, customer information, internal screens, and performance figures are not disclosed.
